description: A tradition — a first-class domain node: an accumulated body of prior knowledge, methods, instruments, and assumptions (colloquially a domain, field, subfield, or research topic; the granularity lives in `level`). Traditions replace domain-as-metadata: as nodes they are participants, not labels — knowledge records hold typed relationships to them (see tech.scios.rrgi.stemsFrom), claims can be made ABOUT them, and lineage distance can be measured against them. Objects are never IN a tradition ('belongs to' is deliberately retired); they stem from traditions (origin, historical, plural) and may later speak to others (relevance — a future relation). The initial set is imported from the OpenAlex topic hierarchy (CC0; topics are citation-community clusters ≈ traditions; labels/descriptions at the topic level are LLM-generated — provenance names the generator, and the import is one institution's attributed lens, not ontological truth). The set is open: a future in-graph-minted tradition (condensed from cross-tradition activity) is this same record with no externalId and its own provenance. The hierarchy is carried by the `parent` field (node-held structural link, the issue.motivatedBy precedent) rather than reified edges: imported ontology structure is one artifact's internal shape, not an agent's contestable assertion about knowledge. RRGI-authored (no DiscourseGraphs coalition equivalent yet); intended to be proposed upstream. See DISCOVERY.md (concept) and notes/discovery-proposal-B-domain-layer.md (design).

text.description: The tradition's display name (e.g. 'Caching and Content Delivery', 'Computer Science').

level.description: The hierarchy level. Open (not closed) so future born-in-graph traditions can carry community-defined levels (e.g. 'emergent').

externalId.description: Scheme-prefixed identifier in the source ontology, e.g. 'openalex:T11986' or 'openalex:subfields/2202' (the canon_key convention applied to ontology ids). Absent on born-in-graph traditions.

parent.description: Dual-addressed reference (URI + CID) to the parent tradition (topic→subfield→field→domain). Absent at the domain level. A structural node-held link, not a reified relation: the hierarchy is imported ontology structure, and the strongRef pins the exact parent version per RRGI's dual-addressing rule.

description.description: What this tradition is. For OpenAlex-imported topics this is the source ontology's (LLM-generated) description — attributed via provenance, contestable like everything else.

tags.description: Keywords (for OpenAlex topics, the source ontology's keyword list).
